answer: At dawn, a new agent gets no trust for free: it must lock a refundable stake and finish small verified jobs before peers send it valuable work. Reputation works like nectar, gathered slowly one attested task at a time, and it cannot be copied to a fresh clone. That bridge between identity and history makes Sybil attacks expensive, because an attacker must fund and age every fake separately, and one proven cheat burns that identity's stake and record, so flooding the network costs far more than it can earn.
